title: Musk rejects rumors of TSMC takeover of Terafab — Intel reaffirms 14A node deal as Musk floats cleanroom 'sublease'
source_used: Tom's Hardware (citing Bloomberg for Intel's chief executive)
key_facts: Intel's chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said Intel will remain part of Terafab, citing Bloomberg, and the remark was made on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 before an Intel event in Japan.
Terafab is the chip-production venture of SpaceX, Tesla and xAI; in April, Intel and Terafab said the new chipmaker would use Intel's 14A process.
Details of the Intel collaboration are still unknown; there is a general understanding that Intel will license its manufacturing technology to Terafab.
Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, Tesla and xAI, denied rumours that Terafab would invest and then partner with TSMC, which would build and operate the fab.
Musk proposed that TSMC could sublease part of Terafab to make chips for its customers.
Tom's Hardware analysis by Anton Shilov, a contributing writer there, calls a TSMC sublease unusual because of different process flows, IP protection and downtime liability.
quote_evidence: Intel will remain a part of Elon Musk's Terafab project, Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, told reporters on Wednesday.
"No, we will build and run the fab," Elon Musk wrote in an X post.
Maybe TSMC subleases part of the Terafab if they want, but nothing more than that.
why_it_matters_hint: Who runs Terafab, and whether TSMC has any role in it, is still unclear; the venture is meant to make chips for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI.
